cands.name: Clyde Jones

top: PROFESSIONAL MUSICIAN WRITER PRODUCER · Charlottesville, VA
pacs: American Postal Workers Union Committee On Political Action
Committee To Elect Shomari Figures For Congress
money.note: Individuals gave $184,952; PAC money $13,000; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Retired U.S. Army First Sergeant with 21 years in the Signal Corps and a Bronze Star. Moved to Alabama in 2013 to work for DuPont, then retired in 2024 from FMC as a Process Safety Management Coordinator. Associate minister in Daphne and former Alabama Arise board president. Democratic nominee, Alabama's 1st District, 2026.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Jones holding elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found nothing on his positions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or out-of-state land buyers, slowing growth or protecting land, policing and public order, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The details of his upbringing were not found, though he attended Charles City High School. The campaign issues page was cut off partway through its veterans section. His endorsements page was not available. Ballotpedia lists only online voter-guide recommendations, which we did not treat as notable endorsements.

qual.background: Served 21 years in the U.S. Army, retiring as a First Sergeant in the Signal Corps. Later worked at DuPont and then at FMC Agriculture Solutions as a Process Safety Management Coordinator until May 2024. He has not held elected office.
qual.why: He has no legislative, executive-office, legal or budget background. His military leadership as a First Sergeant and his corporate safety-coordination role are relevant management experience but not governing experience. Nonprofit and civic board service is not counted.

stop-data-centers.evidence: His campaign site says he supports a moratorium on building new data centers until adequate environmental impact investigations are done, and that constituents should have a say in what comes to their communities.

clean-money.evidence: His campaign site says he is taking no corporate PAC money and that he will support and vote to overturn Citizens United and get corporate PACs out of elections.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site calls for a path to citizenship for undocumented people and says ICE has "gotten out of control" and that lives shouldn't be put on the line to hit arrest quotas. It also says secure borders are important.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Supports a moratorium on building new data centers until adequate environmental impact investigations are conducted. Says constituents should have a say and that water, the power grid and quality of life should not be compromised.

cands.name: Jerry Carl

pacs: The Eye Of The Tiger Political Action Committee
Vulcan Materials Company Political Action Committee

Blue Cross Blue Shield Of Alabama PAC
Elect - The PAC Of The Alabama Farmers Federation
National Automobile Dealers Association Political Action Committee

money.note: Individuals gave $739,241; PAC money $527,559; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Mobile native and businessman who founded companies in healthcare equipment, real estate and timber. Served on the Mobile County Commission 2012–2020, the last two years as president. Represented Alabama's 1st District in the U.S. House 2021–2025, lost the 2024 primary, and ran again in 2026.

controversies.text: Federal records show $25,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $52,750 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump is listed among his endorsers in the 2026 race.
In his 2024 primary, he was endorsed by AIPAC and by a number of Republican state senators and representatives.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Carl was raised beyond his 1977 graduation from Sylacauga High School, or the year he settled in Mobile. We found no statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, school vouchers or teacher pay, or slowing development. His campaign describes him as favoring "pro-growth" policies, but without specifics on land or zoning. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We found no documented foreign ties, and no information on his county commission votes beyond his campaign's own description.

local.label: Roots 90: He was born in Mobile, graduated from Sylacauga High School (Alabama) in 1977, and has run businesses and held county office in Mobile since, but his childhood residence is not spelled out. · Money: 50% of money from District 1 ZIP codes after leaving out land and development money (64% before)

qual.background: Four years in the U.S. House (Appropriations and Natural Resources committees), eight years on the Mobile County Commission including a term as president, and 40+ years as a business founder in healthcare, real estate and timber.
qual.why: Prior legislative and local executive office plus business management experience fits the lawmaking, budgeting and oversight work of the job.
qual.label: Prior legislative and local executive office plus business management experience fits the lawmaking, budgeting and oversight work of the job.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says that on the Mobile County Commission he consistently voted against raising taxes and gave up a taxpayer-funded salary for his first two years. This is not specific to homestead taxes.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Yea on the Secure the Border Act of 2023 (H.R. 2), which limited asylum eligibility and required employers to use electronic work-eligibility verification; the bill passed the House 219-213.

second-amendment.evidence: Voted Nay on the Assault Weapons Ban of 2022 (H.R. 1808), which passed the House 217-213.

pro-life.evidence: Voted Nay on the Women's Health Protection Act of 2021 (H.R. 3755), which would have barred governmental restrictions on abortion services; it passed the House 218-211.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he supports law enforcement, opposes defunding the police, and will "always support cops over criminals."

prio.label: Matches 5 of 5 priorities; 3 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: He was born in Mobile, graduated from Sylacauga High School (Alabama) in 1977, and has run businesses and held county office in Mobile since, but his childhood residence is not spelled out.
